code: # R/derive_liver_flags.R # # One row per subject: age, sex, dose, and peak ALT and AST as a multiple of # the upper limit of normal. Reads its inputs through the set `x`, so it uses # exactly the versions the set pins. derive_liver_flags <- function(x, conn_input) {   dm <- datom_fetch_member(conn = conn_input, x = x, member = "dm")   ex <- datom_fetch_member(conn = conn_input, x = x, member = "ex")   lb <- datom_fetch_member(conn = conn_input, x = x, member = "lb")    peak_xuln <- function(test) {     rows <- lb[lb$LBTESTCD == test, ]     tapply(X = rows$LBORRES / rows$LBORNRHI, INDEX = rows$USUBJID, FUN = max)   }    liver_flags <- merge(     x  = dm[, c("USUBJID", "AGE", "SEX")],     y  = ex[, c("USUBJID", "EXDOSE")],     by = "USUBJID"   )   liver_flags$ALT_PEAK_XULN <- as.numeric(peak_xuln("ALT")[liver_flags$USUBJID])   liver_flags$AST_PEAK_XULN <- as.numeric(peak_xuln("AST")[liver_flags$USUBJID])   liver_flags$ELEVATED <- liver_flags$ALT_PEAK_XULN > 1 |     liver_flags$AST_PEAK_XULN > 1    liver_flags } source(fs::path(workdir_liver_safety, "R", "derive_liver_flags.R"))  x <- datom_get_set(conn = conn_read_liver_safety, name = set_liver_safety)  liver_flags <- derive_liver_flags(x = x, conn_input = conn_read_imported)  liver_flags_written <- datom_write(   conn    = conn_write_liver_safety,   data    = liver_flags,   name    = "liver_flags",   parents = datom_parent(     conn  = conn_read_imported,     table = c("dm", "ex", "lb"),     x     = x   ) ) #> v Wrote "liver_flags" (full): "dafdb954"  x <- datom_add_member(   x       = x,   member  = "liver_flags",   version = liver_flags_written$metadata_sha,   tags    = list(type = "output"),   conn    = conn_read_liver_safety ) #> i Nothing has been written. Write the set with `datom_write_set(conn, x)`.  v2 <- datom_write_set(   conn          = conn_write_liver_safety,   members       = x,   include_paths = "R" ) #> v Wrote set "study001-liver-safety" (5 members): "66d721f3"

title: Tracing Data Lineage
text: datom_write() derives derived table’s source_lineage union parents’ lineages write time, lineage version-pinned. recompute equals recorded value normal operation – difference flags drift corruption worth investigating. dedicated validator; instead compose existing reads datom_lineage_union(). recipe four steps: recipe reads parent connection, extends cross-project parents without change: open connection scoped parent’s project (p$source) read parent . single connection ever expected reach across project stores.
code: # 1. Read the derived table's recorded parents. Each entry carries #    source, table, version, and data_sha -- enough to pick the parent's #    project connection and its pinned version. parents <- datom_get_parents(conn, "dm_clean")  # 2. Read each parent's source_lineage through a connection scoped to that #    parent's project. For same-project parents this is the same `conn`. parent_lineages <- lapply(parents, function(p) {   datom_get_lineage(conn, p$table, version = p$version, depth = "source") })  # 3. Union the parents' lineages (dedup by {project, table, version_sha}). recomputed <- datom_lineage_union(parent_lineages)  # 4. Compare against the derived table's recorded source_lineage. recorded <- datom_get_lineage(conn, "dm_clean", depth = "source") identical(recomputed, recorded) #> [1] TRUE # Cross-project variant: resolve a connection per parent project. parent_lineages <- lapply(parents, function(p) {   parent_conn <- conn_for_project(p$source)   # your connection resolver   datom_get_lineage(parent_conn, p$table, version = p$version,                     depth = "source") }) recomputed <- datom_lineage_union(parent_lineages)

NULL default. gov_root Governance storage root (can NULL legacy conns). gov_prefix Governance prefix (can NULL). gov_region Governance region (can NULL). gov_backend Governance storage backend ("s3" "local"), set governance store component. NULL solo (-governance) conns. Independent backend (data backend): project may keep data one backend governance another. gov_client Governance storage client (can NULL). gov_local_path Absolute path local gov clone (NULL readers). data_repo_url HTTPS URL data GitHub repository. Populated conn-construction time git remote store. NULL readers yet known. github_pat GitHub personal access token held memory . Sourced store$github_pat conn-construction time. Never persisted disk never printed. github_api_url GitHub API base URL. Sourced store$github_api_url conn-construction time. Defaults "https://api.github.com" set. min_writer_version lowest version datom repo accepts writes , read project.yaml conn-construction time. NULL means repo declares limit, every repo written far. Held connection file comes already parsed , write-entry check costs extra read.

code: # Offline, self-contained: a bare git repo stands in for GitHub and a # local directory for object storage. if (requireNamespace("git2r", quietly = TRUE)) {   tmp <- tempfile("datom-example-")   remote <- file.path(tmp, "remote.git")   dir.create(remote, recursive = TRUE)   git2r::init(remote, bare = TRUE)    store <- datom_store(     data = datom_store_local(file.path(tmp, "storage")),     github_pat = "example-token", # role selector; a local remote needs none     data_repo_url = remote,     validate = FALSE   )   datom_init_repo(file.path(tmp, "repo"), "example_project", store)   conn <- datom_get_conn(file.path(tmp, "repo"), store)    print(conn)    unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE) } #> ℹ Created store directory /tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764b6a220c/storage. #> ✔ Initialized datom repository "example_project" at /tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764b6a220c/repo #>  #> ── datom connection  #> • Project: "example_project" #> • Backend: "local" #> • Role: "developer" #> • Data root: "/tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764b6a220c/storage" #> • Governance: not attached #> • Path: /tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764b6a220c/repo #> • Data repo: </tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764b6a220c/remote.git>

code: # Offline, self-contained: a bare git repo stands in for GitHub and a # local directory for object storage. if (requireNamespace("git2r", quietly = TRUE)) {   tmp <- tempfile("datom-example-")   remote <- file.path(tmp, "remote.git")   dir.create(remote, recursive = TRUE)   git2r::init(remote, bare = TRUE)    store <- datom_store(     data = datom_store_local(file.path(tmp, "storage")),     github_pat = "example-token", # role selector; a local remote needs none     data_repo_url = remote,     validate = FALSE   )   datom_init_repo(file.path(tmp, "repo"), "example_project", store)   conn <- datom_get_conn(file.path(tmp, "repo"), store)    datom_write(conn, data = datom_example_data("dm"), name = "dm")   print(datom_summary(conn))    unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE) } #> ℹ Created store directory /tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764d854c94/storage. #> ✔ Initialized datom repository "example_project" at /tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764d854c94/repo #> ✔ Wrote "dm" (full): "b5cbba45" #>  #> ── datom project summary  #> • Project: "example_project" #> • Role: "developer" #> • Backend: local -- "/tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764d854c94/storage" #> • Tables: 1 (1 version total) #> • Sets: 0 #> • Last write: "2026-10-03T21:07:05Z" #> • Remote: "/tmp/Rtmpvh48Dj/datom-example-1a764d854c94/remote.git"

what: Table identity: the datom-cv1 canonical hash
title: datom 0.1.1
text: Table identity defined canonical hash table’s values (datom-cv1), bytes parquet serialization. Hashing serialization tied identity writer: arrow upgrade different compression default produced different bytes identical data, therefore spurious new version. See vignette("design-version-shas") model identity decisions. Pre-release data_sha values change, migration path. table written pre-release build carries data_sha computed old algorithm. values recomputed, converted, reconciled — pilots re-onboard data. Three SHAs now recorded per table: data_sha (content identity), metadata_sha (version pass datom_read(version = )), parquet_sha (stored object’s SHA-256, verified read parsing). metadata.json gains hash_algo, parquet_sha, column_hashes — ordered per-column digest index data_sha can re-derived without downloading data.
